cards.name: Gaussian Blur
cards.summary: Photoshop-style Gaussian blur applied as a live raster effect: the whole object or group goes uniformly soft and out of focus, and its edges fade into soft semi-transparent halos that spread past the original outline. Radius (the blur key) sets how far it spreads; at 10 the harvest probe rectangle got a visibly soft edge.
use_for: soft out-of-focus background shapes or bokeh blobs behind a headline
a glow: a blurred, coloured copy of type or a logo stacked under the sharp one in the Appearance panel
fake depth of field in flat illustrations (blur the far layers)
soft shadows and light pools built from a blurred dark or light shape
smooth colour blends from a few blurred blobs (mesh-gradient look)
avoid: type or logos that must stay readable: blur a copy under the sharp original instead
a soft shadow under an object: Effect > Stylize > Drop Shadow does it with offset and opacity built in
softening only the outline while the inside stays sharp: use Effect > Stylize > Feather
print work at a low Document Raster Effects Settings resolution: the blurred raster turns blocky; set 300 ppi and re-check the look after any change to that setting

params.name: blur
params.does: Radius: how far each point spreads; larger = softer and wider halo past the edges
params.typical: 10 (dialog value at harvest) gave the probe rectangle about 7 px of soft edge; 30 or more for a strong blur, much higher turns shapes into colour clouds

pairs_with: Effect > Stylize > Outer Glow / Inner Glow
Transparency panel blend modes (Screen, Multiply) on the blurred copy
Effect > Document Raster Effects Settings (raise to 300 ppi for print)
cards.scripting: item.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="Adobe PSL Gaussian Blur"><Dict data="R PrevDocScale 1.0 B NeedHighResExecution 0 I PrevDres 300 R blur 30.0"/></LiveEffect>')  // menu route: select the art, app.executeMenuCommand("Live Adobe PSL Gaussian Blur") opens the dialog (needs an OK)
cards.non_destructive: yes: live effect, listed in the Appearance panel and re-editable by double-clicking it there; Object > Expand Appearance (or Object > Rasterize) bakes it into an embedded image
cards.cost: medium: raster effect at the Document Raster Effects resolution, re-rendered on every edit; large radii on big art slow redraw noticeably

review.changes: blur typical: '10-30 strong blur' contradicted the harvest render (blur 10 = about 7 px of soft edge on Effect_Blur_Gaussian_Blur.png), now cites the harvested 10

verified.note: At blur 30 the whole vector plate goes uniformly soft and out of focus with soft halos spreading past every outline, the type and zigzag smeared, as the card says.

cards.name: Radial Blur
cards.summary: Photoshop Radial Blur as a live effect: Spin smears the art along concentric circles around a centre point, like a spinning wheel; Zoom smears it along lines radiating from the centre, a zoom-burst / speed-rush look. Amount sets the streak length, Quality trades speed for smoothness (Draft is grainy).
use_for: zoom-burst speed streaks behind a sale or sports headline (Zoom)
spinning wheel, fan, vinyl or turbine motion (Spin)
high-energy poster and thumbnail backgrounds from simple shapes
a sense of rushing toward the viewer on an icon or logo mark (Zoom)
avoid: straight-line motion: Illustrator's Blur menu has no Motion Blur; make it in Photoshop (Motion Blur)
final art at Draft quality: the streaks look noisy; use Good or Best
precise placement of the centre: Center is set by dragging in the dialog's preview box

scripted output with chosen values: a plain applyEffect stores the effect but draws nothing by itself (harvest render diff 0.0); use the menu command and its dialog, a graphic style saved with the values, or the gallery route (see scripting), which renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog

params.name: Amount
params.does: length of the spin arc or zoom streak
params.typical: 10 (dialog value at harvest) visibly spun the probe's corners; 30-50 for strong streaks

params.name: Method
params.does: Spin (circular smear around the centre) or Zoom (streaks radiating from it)
params.typical: Zoom for speed / impact, Spin for rotation (CorelDRAW splits them: Effects/Blur/Zoom and Effects/Blur/Radial Blur)

params.name: Quality
params.does: Draft is fast but grainy; Good and Best are smoother and slower
params.typical: good while designing, best for final

params.name: Center
params.does: the blur centre, dragged in the dialog's preview box
params.typical: middle of the art; offset it toward a focal point

pairs_with: Effect > Blur > Gaussian Blur on a copy for extra softness
a sharp copy of the same art on top, so the streaks read as motion trails
cards.scripting: select the art, then app.executeMenuCommand("Live PSAdapter_plugin_RdlB")  // opens the Radial Blur dialog with its last-used values and needs an OK; Amount, Method (Spin / Zoom), Quality and Center are set there. The harvest dropped the applyEffect route: a scripted applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="PSAdapter_plugin_RdlB">...') stored the effect but drew nothing by itself (no settings reach it that way) (render diff 0.0 vs 1.517 for the menu route). Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).
cards.non_destructive: yes: live effect, listed in the Appearance panel and re-editable by double-clicking it there; Object > Expand Appearance (or Object > Rasterize) bakes it into an embedded image
cards.cost: medium-high: raster effect re-rendered on every edit; Best quality and large amounts are slow on big art

review.changes: removed 'CorelDRAW Effects/Blur/Zoom' from pairs_with (a CorelDRAW effect cannot be paired inside Illustrator; the note moved to the Method param); Amount typical '40-100' implied the unharvested max, now cites the harvested 10 and the menu-route render

verified.note: Zoom at Amount 40 smears the photo, strip and ramp along lines radiating from the centre, a clear zoom-burst look as the card describes; the frame was drawn by the gallery's scripted route, so the 'only the menu command renders it' avoid line was corrected.

cards.name: Smart Blur
cards.summary: Photoshop Smart Blur as a live effect: blurs only low-contrast areas (pixel differences below Threshold, within Radius) and keeps high-contrast edges sharp, so grain and soft gradients smooth out while outlines stay crisp. Edge Only mode replaces the art with white edge lines on black; Overlay Edge draws those white edge lines over the art. On flat vector fills Normal mode changes almost nothing.
use_for: smoothing grain or noise in raster effects and placed images while keeping edges
a clean, simplified, slightly posterised look on textured art
white-outline line-art look over shapes (Overlay Edge)
white-on-black edge trace of a logo or illustration (Edge Only)
avoid: visible softening of flat vector shapes: Normal mode does almost nothing there (harvest menu-route render differed from the plain rectangle by only 0.048); use Gaussian Blur
Edge Only when the colours must survive: it replaces the art with black and white lines

scripted output with chosen values: a plain applyEffect stores the effect but draws nothing by itself (harvest render diff 0.0); use the menu command and its dialog, a graphic style saved with the values, or the gallery route (see scripting), which renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog

params.name: Radius
params.does: how far it looks for similar pixels to blur together
params.typical: 3 (dialog value at harvest); 10 for a stronger effect

params.name: Threshold
params.does: how different pixels may be and still get blurred; higher blurs more, lower keeps more detail (and, in the edge modes, detects more edges)
params.typical: 25 (dialog value at harvest); 40 catches only clear colour boundaries

params.name: Quality
params.does: Low / Medium / High smoothness of the result
params.typical: High for final

params.name: Mode
params.does: Normal blurs; Edge Only draws white edges on black; Overlay Edge draws the white edges over the art
params.typical: Normal for smoothing; Overlay Edge for a line-art look

pairs_with: Effect > Blur > Gaussian Blur when a uniform blur is wanted
Transparency panel Screen mode on an Edge Only copy for glowing outlines

Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).

cards.cost: medium: raster effect re-rendered on every edit; High quality with a large radius is slow on big art

cards.name: Accented Edges

cards.cost: medium: raster effect rendered at the Document Raster Effects resolution (300 ppi at harvest) and re-rendered on every edit of the art; the Effect Gallery dialog is slow to preview on large artboards
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Brush Strokes effect that traces and accentuates the edges of the art with a painted stroke line: a high Edge Brightness makes the accents look like white chalk, a low one like black ink. Fills keep their colour with a slight painterly smoothing.
use_for: chalkboard-style white outlines on flat illustrations (high Edge Brightness)
inked, hand-drawn edge emphasis on shapes and type (low Edge Brightness)
textured, painterly poster art from clean vector shapes
avoid: CMYK documents: the Effect Gallery and its Brush Strokes effects are greyed out there; switch File > Document Color Mode to RGB, or do the work in Photoshop

scripted output with chosen values: Edge Width / Edge Brightness / Smoothness cannot be sent by a plain applyEffect; use the menu command and its dialog, or the gallery route (see scripting), which renders the chosen values
print work at a low Effect > Document Raster Effects Settings resolution: the stroke texture is rendered at that resolution and looks coarse or blocky when printed; set 300 ppi before final output
small text: the edge strokes swallow thin letterforms

params.does: thickness of the accented edge line
params.typical: 2 (dialog value at harvest) fine, 6-8 bold

params.typical: 38 (dialog value at harvest); near the top for white chalk, near 0 for black ink

params.name: Smoothness
params.does: how smooth the edge lines are; higher = fewer, cleaner strokes
params.typical: 5 (dialog value at harvest); lower for rougher, more numerous strokes

Object > Expand Appearance, then Object > Image Trace for a vector result

cards.name: Dark Strokes

cards.summary: Filter Gallery Brush Strokes effect that paints dark areas with short, tight dark strokes and light areas with long white strokes, pushing the art toward a high-contrast, moody painted look; Black and White Intensity set how far the darks and lights are driven.
use_for: moody, dramatic painterly poster art
gritty, high-contrast editorial or noir illustration
adding stroke texture and punch to flat colour shapes
avoid: CMYK documents: the Effect Gallery and its Brush Strokes effects are greyed out there; switch File > Document Color Mode to RGB, or do the work in Photoshop
art whose colours must stay true: dark colours go near black and light ones toward white
small text and fine detail: strokes clog it
print work at a low Effect > Document Raster Effects Settings resolution: the stroke texture is rendered at that resolution and looks coarse or blocky when printed; set 300 ppi before final output

flat vector fills: on flat or very smooth art this filter has nothing to stroke and only remaps brightness, so at these values every colour without a channel at 255 (gradients, dark greys, a flat red) goes solid black while fills with a full channel (pure orange, pure blue) survive; that is Illustrator's own result (a dialog-applied control matched the scripted render pixel for pixel), so give it a photo or textured art

cards.name: Sprayed Strokes
cards.non_destructive: yes: live effect, listed in the Appearance panel and re-editable by double-clicking it there; Object > Expand Appearance (or Object > Rasterize) bakes it into an embedded image
cards.cost: medium: raster effect rendered at the Document Raster Effects resolution (300 ppi at harvest) and re-rendered on every edit of the art; the Effect Gallery dialog is slow to preview on large artboards
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Brush Strokes effect that repaints the art with its dominant colours in long, angled, sprayed streaks running in one chosen direction (right or left diagonal, horizontal, vertical), like spray paint or wind-blown rain; edges smear into streaky trails.
use_for: street-art / spray-can texture on shapes and type
rain-streak or wind-swept painterly backgrounds
directional motion texture on flat colour art
avoid: CMYK documents: the Effect Gallery and its Brush Strokes effects are greyed out there; switch File > Document Color Mode to RGB, or do the work in Photoshop

scripted output with chosen values: Stroke Length / Spray Radius / Stroke Direction cannot be sent by a plain applyEffect; use the menu command and its dialog, or the gallery route (see scripting), which renders the chosen values
exactly repeatable output: a random seed changes the spray on every application
small text: the streaks smear it beyond legibility
print work at a low Effect > Document Raster Effects Settings resolution: the stroke texture is rendered at that resolution and looks coarse or blocky when printed; set 300 ppi before final output

params.name: Stroke Length
params.does: length of each sprayed streak
params.typical: 12 (dialog value at harvest); 18 long streaks

params.name: Spray Radius
params.does: how widely colour is sprayed around each streak
params.typical: 7 (dialog value at harvest); 20 wide spray

params.name: Stroke Direction
params.does: direction the streaks run
params.typical: Right Diagonal; Horizontal or Vertical for wind / rain

pairs_with: Effect > Brush Strokes > Spatter for ragged edges as well
a sharp copy of the art on top for a motion-trail look
